newsitem.title: USA: New England utilities agree on transmission.
newsitem.headline: New England utilities agree on transmission.

text.p: The New England Power Pool said the top executives of its member companies have agreed in principle to restructure power transmission in the region and create a New England Independent System Operator.
NEPOOL said its Executive Committee agreed in principle on the most fundamental restructuring issues facing competitive power markets in New England.
Involved in that agreement were reprsentatives of New England Electric System, Northeast Utilities, Commonwealth Energy System, Central Maine Power Co and Boston Edison Co units.

NEPOOL spokesman William P. Sheperdson said the committee also includes United Illuminating Co and representatives of Massachusetts' municipal utilities, Vermont's investor owned utilities -- Central Vermont Public Service Corp, Green Mountain Power Corp and Rochester Electric Light & Power Co, other small investor owned utilities in the region -- Nantucket Electric Co, Bozrah Light and Power Co and Bangor Hydro-Electric Co and power marketers such as Enron Corp.
Sheperdson said it is "most likely" the ISO will be separate from NEPOOL.

NEPOOL Executive Committee Chairman Frank P. Sabatino said the agreement reached on Monday was a "true landmark consensus, one which would ultimately benefit all players in the regional wholesale power markets, as well as their customers."
Sheperdson pointed out there had been no concensus on regional transmission since before Northeast Utilities' acquisition of Public Service of New Hampshire.

"The agreement provides for balanced participation in the governance of NEPOOL, a non-discriminatory regional transmission tariff and the criteria of competitive markets for energy, capacity and ancillary services," Sabatino said.
The official expects a filing will be made with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission by the year-end to seek approval of these changes.
